newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 14.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 14.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Monday:
* Foreign investors are likely to lead a rally in the Manila equities market on Monday as the weaker peso and bargain prices will serve as natural lure to bargain hunters, brokers said.
However, some brokers said any rally might be tempered by profit-taking.
* "It's a double buy for the Philippines. We have very cheap peso and at the same time, bargain stocks," Noel Reyes, vice president of Anscor-Hagedorn Securities, said.
He said the buying momentum triggered by the de facto peso devaluation last Friday could push the index to 2,800 in the near-term.
On Friday, the composite index surged 189.99 points, or 7.57 percent, to close at 2,701.14. The peso fell to a 45-month low of 29.45 to the U.S. dollar before bankers suspended trading.
* BPI analyst Spencer Yap said export firms and dollar-earners should benefit from the sharp peso depreciation, while property firms should expect briskier sales due to the declining interest rates.

On the other hand, companies reliant on imports such as food firms, and companies with heavy dollar-denominated debts, such as banks, telecom firms and conglomerates, might suffer from the weak peso regime.
"We expect investors to take the opportunity to realign portfolios; the expected revaluation of corporate earnings prospects may see any upward rally tempered," Yap said.
* Asian Capital Equities Inc also warned that the market was prone to profit taking.

"The stock market will be prone to profit-taking, having gone up sharply in a single day. Renewed speculation as to the new peso level might keep our stock market drifting aimlessly in the next few days," Asian Capital Equities in a report said.
* On Friday, the Dow Jones rose 35.06 points to 7,921.82.
* The interbank call loan rate inched up slightly to 32.5625 percent amid a slight turnover of 9.548 billion pesos.
* Government officials and industry leaders urged businessmen not to take advantage of the sharp peso fall, saying that the peso value will normalise within the next few days.
* BusinessWorld says the Philippine Stock Exchange is stuyding a tighter trading quota for stock market agents to encourage professionalism.
